scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The duplicate registration problem
scenes.caption: Asha receives two fictional tables: registrations and check-ins. Two different people share the name Riya. One registration ID has conflicting statuses, one check-in repeats and another check-in has no matching registration.
scenes.dialogue: A name match cannot resolve these records.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: The join can hide a problem
scenes.caption: Joining on names could merge different people. A unique registration ID should identify one registration, and a check-in reference should point to that ID. The supplied dirty tables violate those intended constraints and need reconciliation first.
scenes.dialogue: Do not silently overwrite a key conflict.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Keep unresolved cases visible
scenes.caption: Group by stable ID, preserve original rows and classify conflicts, repeated check-ins and unmatched references. A registration with no check-in row has unknown attendance; an absent row is not proof that the person was absent.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Choose the reconciliation rule
scenes.caption: Should the team merge all Riya rows, keep whichever conflicting value arrived last, or reconcile by stable ID and hold unresolved cases for authorised review?
scenes.dialogue: Preserve the conflict instead of guessing.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: An evidence-linked result
scenes.caption: Asha keeps R02 and R03 distinct despite their shared name. The conflicting R02 values, repeated R01 check-in and unmatched R05 reference remain visible. R04 matches; R03 has no check-in evidence.
scenes.dialogue: The unresolved list is part of the output.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Enter the reconciliation lab
scenes.caption: Define the key relationships, run the supplied join audit and classify every result. Explain the human review needed before a repaired key or attendance conclusion is accepted.
scenes.dialogue: A reliable join starts with reliable identity.
